summary: You have built a coherent sun-synchronous Earth-observation concept, and your STK access results and ground track give useful software evidence. Your introduction clearly explains the mission and the single-satellite choice. The report is currently at Adequate overall. Correcting the orbital elements, completing the end-of-life plan, and strengthening references and presentation will move it towards Accomplished.
next_steps: Correct the classical orbital elements table: define the argument of latitude properly rather than stating 0° while calling it undefined, justify the RAAN from the launch site, and state the sun-synchronous precession as 0.9856°/day.

Complete the end-of-life section by finishing the truncated drag-sail sentence and adding a quantitative decay estimate for 600 km that reconciles it with the no-thrust constraint. Replace the Wikipedia source with authoritative references and cite them consistently.

Resolve the launch and ground-station inconsistencies: explain the launch-site latitude against the 97.8° retrograde inclination, name the operator explicitly, and make pass counts and contact durations match the access table, removing the duplicated access 13.

criteria.C1: You clearly state the primary mission, why it is needed, the single-satellite choice, and government and science users such as CSIRO and BOM. To reach Accomplished, name the operator explicitly, separate operator from customers, and support claims with stronger literature. Remove weakly sourced statements, such as the 30% acidity claim, unless you can reference them properly.
criteria.C2: Your orbit analysis, STK access results and ground track provide good software evidence. The orbital elements contain errors, the Vega E choice and launch-site logic need clearer justification, and the end-of-life section is incomplete. Give delta-v for any maneuvers, and justify ground stations in line with your Australian focus. Accomplished work needs accurate, fully justified decisions supported by quantitative evidence throughout.
criteria.C3: You reach sensible conclusions, such as the illumination benefit of a polar sun-synchronous orbit, and you acknowledge launch uncertainty. These largely restate the design. Add quantified outcomes, critically weigh trade-offs such as a single satellite against a constellation, and assess end-of-life risk to reach a detailed, evidence-based conclusion.
criteria.C4: Your clear headings and labelled figures give the report a logical structure. Improve consistency by correcting the duplicated table entry and contents page errors, fixing typos and grammar, completing truncated sentences, and using one citation style with access dates for web sources. Replacing the Wikipedia reference will also help meet the brief.
